summary: A 1934 100-foot steel Aermotor tower on Elk Summit near Elk City, Idaho; the Forest Service says it is not accessible to the public and not currently used by the agency.

facts.design: 100-foot steel Aermotor (MC-40) tower with 7 by 7 ft cab, built 1934 on a summit that has had a lookout since 1911 (crow's nest first)

staffing.status: not currently used by the Forest Service (NHLR says used as needed by Elk City Ranger District)

access.note: Forest Service: tower remains intact, is not currently used, and is not accessible by the public

visit.trail_note: Forest Service gives road directions from State Highway 14 (Forest Roads 1199 and 417), but states the tower is not accessible by the public

corrections.why: NHLR describes a 100-foot tower and the Forest Lookouts page gives a 100-foot Aermotor; 2.1 m does not match any source gathered

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 6,365 ft (1,940 m); the Forest Service page, firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 6,386 ft. The record's 1940.1 m matches NHLR only. Both figures are reported, so no change is proposed.

notes_for_editor: Record height 2.1 m is wrong; sources give a 100-foot tower (proposed 30.5 m). Status is disputed: NHLR (undated page) says used as needed by the Elk City Ranger District, while the Forest Service page (updated June 4, 2025) says not currently used by the agency and not accessible to the public. The story reports both and does not resolve it; the NHLR wording may be older. An Idaho County Free Press feature on the lookout (idahocountyfreepress.com, 88-year-old lookout tower article) was returned by search but could not be read (HTTP 429); it may say more about current use and should be checked by a human. Elevation: see resolved_conflicts. Access is closed per the Forest Service; no climbing advice given.
